parts.objective: Compare the objectives of minimizing travel time for all nodes versus maximizing points of interest within a defined time threshold

key_points.text: The new approach aims to find an optimal path covering the maximum number of points of interest (POIs) under a specific time constraint (TTH).
The minimum time required for an optimal tour may still exceed the threshold that causes cyber sickness.
The Time Threshold (TTH) is established to restrict the user's VR exposure time to prevent the possibility of cyber sickness.
A time threshold can be determined through empirical studies, depending on content, or by utilizing pre-existing study results.
When optimizing for maximum POIs under a time threshold, it is not required to visit every single node or vertex.

terms.name: Cyber sickness
terms.definition: Cyber sickness is a possibility or condition that can occur in a virtual system, particularly if the user's movement time or VR exposure time exceeds a defined threshold.

terms.name: Optimal path
terms.definition: An optimal path is a specific route within the virtual world that satisfies the chosen objective. This path is either designed to cover all vertices in minimum time or to cover the maximum number of points of interest within a fixed time limit.

terms.name: Time threshold
terms.definition: A time threshold is a defined maximum duration (or time limit) for the user's movement or VR experience. By restricting movement within this threshold, the risk of cyber sickness is minimized.

parts.objective: Formulate and define a problem to maximize the total importance of a path within a given time threshold

key_points.text: Node importance is quantified using an importance function $f_v$, which maps a vertex (or point of interest) $V$ to a positive real number (37, 38).
The total importance of a path $P$ is defined as the summation of the individual importance of all nodes $f_{P} = Σ f_{vi}$ (45).
The goal is to maximize the total path importance ($F_p$) while ensuring the path is completed within a time threshold ($TH$) (47, 48).
A larger positive real number indicates a higher importance for a node (40).

terms.name: Importance of every node
terms.definition: The importance of every node is a positive real number assigned to each vertex or point of interest. A higher number indicates a higher level of importance.

terms.name: Time threshold
terms.definition: The time threshold is the maximum allowable time that a given path can be completed within, serving as the constraint in the optimization problem.

terms.name: Importance function
terms.definition: The importance function is a computational tool used to assign or compute an importance value to every vertex, mapping each vertex to a positive real number.

terms.name: Vertex
terms.definition: A vertex is every point of interest in the system, which is mapped to a positive real number to indicate its specific importance.

terms.surface: total importance of a given path
terms.name: Total importance of a given path
terms.definition: The total importance of a given path is a summation of the individual importance of every node contained within that specific path.

parts.objective: Define and calculate waiting time and integrate it into a constrained path optimization problem

key_points.text: Waiting time is the time required for a user to inspect or interact with an object at a specific point of interest (node) (52).
A waiting time function, W, maps each node (V) to a real positive number representing the maximum interaction time required at that node (54, 56).
Total waiting time for a path (W_P) is the summation of the individual waiting times of all nodes in that path (60).
The revised problem objective is to maximize total importance (F_P) while ensuring the total travel time plus total waiting time does not exceed a time threshold (T_threshold) (63, 64).

terms.name: Waiting time
terms.definition: Waiting time is the maximum time a user requires to inspect or interact with a particular object at a node that is the point of interest.

terms.name: Waiting time function
terms.definition: The waiting time function is defined as W, which maps every node to a real positive number indicating the maximum time required to inspect or interact with the object at that node.

terms.name: Total waiting time
terms.definition: The total waiting time for a path P is calculated as the summation of the individual waiting times associated with all the nodes along that path.

parts.objective: Formulate a path that maximizes the importance of visited POIs while adhering to a time threshold

key_points.text: VRP with Profit (VRPP) is a generalization of the known Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP).
The core objective is to maximize the total importance (profit) of nodes visited within a given time constraint.
Pathfinding solutions must ensure the user's exposure time remains below a specific threshold to prevent cybersickness.

terms.name: Vehicle routing problem
terms.definition: The vehicle routing problem is a well-known problem that the current topic, VRP with profit, is a generalization of.

terms.name: Vehicle routing problem with profit
terms.definition: VRP with profit is a problem where, instead of needing to visit all nodes, the goal is to maximize profit within given time constraints.

terms.name: Threshold time
terms.definition: Threshold time is the maximum allowable time constraint, defined as the time beyond which a user may experience cybersickness, and the optimized path must restrict user exposure below this limit.

parts.objective: Apply the multi-stage algorithm to find the optimal VR path by incorporating waiting time and importance

key_points.text: The algorithm starts by taking an original graph G (with importance $f$ and waiting time $w$) and aims to find an optimal path P (subject).
The first step involves converting the original graph to a complete graph $G''$ by replacing non-connected edges with shortest paths (subject).
The second step replaces Euclidean distance edges in the complete graph with travel time $t$, computed using the natural walking model (subject).
The VRPP solver uses the final modified graph, importance ($F$), and waiting time ($W$) to output the optimal path $P_{opt}$ (subject).

terms.name: Algorithm
terms.definition: The algorithm is a multi-stage process that creates a graph, converts it into a complete graph with specific edge weights, uses a solver to find the optimal path, and finally modifies the output to reflect the original graph structure.

terms.name: Graph
terms.definition: A graph is a representation of the virtual environment that has a vertex set (V) and an edge set (E). Nodes within the graph can be assigned specific properties like importance and waiting time.

terms.name: Complete graph
terms.definition: A complete graph is a modified version of the original graph where edges that were not originally directly connected are replaced with the shortest path between those vertices.

terms.name: Optimal path
terms.definition: The optimal path is the path chosen from the virtual environment that maximizes the number of highly important points of interest (POIs) while ensuring the total exposure time remains below the time threshold.

terms.name: Total exposure time
terms.definition: The total exposure time represents the sum of the traveling time and the waiting time, and this total must remain below the defined time threshold.

terms.name: Euclidean distance
terms.definition: Euclidean distance is the original measure of distance between two nodes used in the modified graph before the edge weights are replaced with the actual travel time.

terms.name: Travel time
terms.definition: Travel time is the duration of movement between two nodes, which is computed using the natural walking model to give a realistic experience in the virtual world.

terms.name: Natural walking model
terms.definition: The natural walking model is a method used to compute the travel time between nodes, ensuring that the duration reflects a realistic walking experience.

terms.name: VRPP solver
terms.definition: The VRPP solver is the function used to find the optimal path, taking the modified graph, the importance values (F), and the waiting times (W) as inputs.

terms.name: Shortest path
terms.definition: Shortest path is an edge introduced to link nodes that were not originally connected in the virtual world graph to reflect the original nature of the graph.

terms.name: Node
terms.definition: Node is an important location within the virtual environment whose number the optimal path seeks to maximize while adhering to time constraints.

parts.objective: Explain how to formulate an optimal path that maximizes coverage of important Points of Interest within a given time threshold

key_points.text: Simply finding the minimum time path in a virtual environment may not solve cyber sickness issues because the time may still be too large.
Experience optimization requires a refined path formulation that utilizes node weights, node importance, and waiting times.
An optimal path is defined as one that allows the user to cover the maximum number of the most important POIs within a given time limit.

terms.name: Graph representation
terms.definition: A graph representation is a representation of a virtual environment used to identify an optimal path.

terms.name: Optimal path
terms.definition: An optimal path is a route formulated to maximize the number of important Points of Interest covered by a user while operating within a defined time threshold.

terms.name: Node importance
terms.definition: Node importance is a factor incorporated into the optimal path formulation that determines the priority of different points (nodes) in the virtual environment.

terms.name: Time threshold
terms.definition: A time threshold is a maximum allowed time limit within which the user must be able to cover the chosen optimal path.

terms.name: Point of interest
terms.definition: A Point of Interest (POI) is a location within the virtual environment that the user needs to cover, and the optimization goal is to maximize the number of these important points covered.
